draft.title: Australia's trading partners
card: Trade partners are the countries Australia buys from and sells to. Early in the 20th century, most of Australia's trade was with Britain and Europe.
Since the mid 20th century, trade has shifted towards Asia. Asian economies grew fast and wanted Australian resources and other goods and services.
China is now Australia's largest trading partner. Japan, South Korea and the United States follow among the major partners.
Relying heavily on a few partners means a downturn in one of them can affect Australia's exports and income.
draft.remember: Australia's trade has moved from Britain and Europe towards Asia, with China the largest partner.

a.q: Which description best fits the change in Australia's trade patterns since the mid 20th century?
opts: A shift from Britain and Europe towards Asia
A shift from Asia towards Britain and Europe
A shift from the United States towards Japan
A shift from Asia towards the United States
a.why: Asian economies grew quickly and bought more Australian goods, while Britain and Europe became less central. The reverse options get the direction wrong.
a.clue: Think about which region's economies grew fastest.

b.q: Which of these countries is Australia's largest trading partner?
b.why: China is Australia's largest trading partner. Japan, South Korea and the United States are major partners, but each trades less with Australia than China does.
b.clue: It is in Asia and has the largest trade of all.

a.best: A shift from Britain and Europe towards Asia
